q: After intense exercise, breathing rate stays raised for several minutes. Which best explains this 'oxygen debt'?
options: Extra O2 is used to convert lactate back to pyruvate/glucose and to restore ATP and O2 stores
Extra O2 is needed so that muscle cells can convert the CO2 they released back into glucose
Lactate has to be exhaled through the lungs as a gas, which requires deeper and faster breathing
O2 is needed to restart glycolysis, which stops completely during intense exercise
explanation: Lactate is carried in the blood to the liver, where it is converted back to pyruvate and then either respired aerobically or made into glucose/glycogen – processes that need ATP from aerobic respiration. Extra O2 also reoxygenates myoglobin and haemoglobin and restores ATP and creatine phosphate. Lactate is not exhaled, and glycolysis never stops.
